research-report.title: Chronomancer + Mace Offense Evidence Dossier for Randomancer

generationFindings.candidateDiscoveryPolicy: Every Offense records all requested candidate classes; empty arrays mean no publishable candidate survived rather than an imposed quota. Tags were retrieval hints only; prose follows typed catalog relationships plus current research semantics.
excludedContent: Critical Hits is inventory-present but explicitly non-rollable.
Twisted Empyrean and Starborn Onslaught were researched but omitted because the catalog places Twisted Empyrean in the Kalguuran Mace slot, conflicting with the permanent-content exclusion policy.
Repository-only unique routes without current external verification were not published.
staleOrContradictedLocalMechanics: Rapid River is removed/replaced; Now and Again applies to Cascadable and Repeatable spells, not generic Mace attacks.
Inevitable Agony uses its reworked hit-tracking behavior, not old Curse-like semantics.
Perfect Strike no longer always Ignites.
Shockwave Totem no longer follows its obsolete ordinary-support model.
Ancestral Bond now doubles Totem Limit and reserves 75 Spirit per Totem.
catalogGaps: Item-granted skills are excluded from the ordinary craftable-skill surface.
The non-skill selector excludes keystones, hiding Giant’s Blood, Crimson Assault, and Ancestral Bond.
The Three Dragons positive cross-element Shock route and Blistering Bond Bleed bridge are incompletely represented.
Substantial retained prose/passive evidence remains unstructured or stale-looking.
One-handed Mace offhand definitions differ between local sources.
unresolvedResearchQuestions: Whether Twisted Empyrean should remain seasonal-excluded in the current release content policy.
Current externally verified modifiers for repository-only Mace uniques such as Nebuloch, Brain Rattler, Olrovasara, Chober Chaber, and Blistering Bond.
A current independently verified first-Shock support/passive for a generic Lightning Attunement route.
Whether any integrated Mace-causes-Companion bridge now exists.
Exact live offhand legality for unusual one-handed-Mace pairings.

setupAndPayoffRelationships: Glory required -> Hammer of the Gods

solutions.title: Measured Physical Slams
solutions.interpretation: Build around [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemRollingSlam|Rolling Slam]] as the repeatable physical Mace attack, reserving the largest openings for a heavier slam rather than inventing an elemental bridge. [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyInevitableAgony|Inevitable Agony]] materially rewards the hit lane: large impacts feed its tracked life-loss effect, while damage-over-time is not being credited here. The loop is to control spacing, land the two-stage slam, and use [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTimeFreeze|Time Freeze]] when a dangerous target would otherwise punish the commitment. Scale the weapon's physical base, attack and slam damage, area, and only the speed modifiers the chosen attack actually accepts. A shield gives the most forgiving one-handed version; a two-handed Mace raises the hit ceiling but makes positioning and recovery more important. [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTemporalRift|Temporal Rift]] can rewind a bad engagement and clear delayed damage when paired with the appropriate Chronomancer defensive path. Hammer of the Gods may be a burst addition, but only after a real Glory engine exists; neither Time Snap nor generic cooldown language supplies Glory.
solutions.defense: Shield for consistency, or two-handed Mace with Phased Form and Temporal Rift supporting close-range commitments.
caveats: Do not assume Hammer of the Gods is available without Glory.

setupAndPayoffRelationships: Forge Hammer cooldown -> Time Snap reset

solutions.title: Perfect Fire Window
solutions.interpretation: The build turns a strong physical Mace base into a deliberate Fire hit with [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemPerfectStrike|Perfect Strike]], rather than treating Fire as an incidental ailment tag. Release the timed strike in the safe window created by [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable7|Apex of the Moment]]; its enemy slow helps with positioning but is not described as a damage multiplier. [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyInevitableAgony|Inevitable Agony]] then gives the large hit a Chronomancer-specific payoff. Improve weapon physical damage first because the skill converts from that base, followed by Fire or elemental attack scaling and relevant penetration. Ignite is not required for this solution and is intentionally absent: current Perfect Strike does not retain its obsolete always-Ignite behavior. In play, clear with measured strikes, save perfect timing for rares and bosses, and avoid overcommitting merely because the target is slowed. A shield smooths the timing exercise, while a two-handed Mace emphasizes the single impact. Temporal defensive tools are valuable for melee recovery, but the route's identity remains a converted Fire hit, not a generic Chronomancer template.
solutions.defense: Prefer a shield while learning the release window; heavier two-handed versions need stronger mitigation and recovery.
caveats: Perfect Strike must not be described as always Igniting.

solutions.title: Forge Hammer Cooldown Cycle
solutions.interpretation: Use [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemForgeHammer|Forge Hammer]] to establish an embedded Fire hammer, then work its recall or nearby-Warcry shatter loop to produce the fissure payoff. This is a Mace-native Fire route with a real cooldown rhythm, so [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTimeSnap|Time Snap]] contributes specifically by resetting the cooldown when an immediate recast matters; it does not replace the skill's recall interaction or create any missing Warcry setup. The player alternates placement, ordinary Mace pressure, and shatter timing instead of repeating one attack. Scale the physical weapon base that feeds conversion, Fire attack and area damage, and enough speed or control to place the hammer safely. Because the build spends time close to an embedded object, positional recovery is more valuable than simply maximizing tooltip damage. A shield can stabilize the setup loop, while a two-handed weapon pushes the impact. This route stays distinct from Perfect Strike by making cooldown and object management—not release timing—the central Chronomancer interaction.
solutions.defense: Use block or another dependable hit layer; keep Temporal Rift available when hammer placement leaves poor positioning.
caveats: Time Snap resets cooldowns but does not satisfy other prerequisites.

solutions.title: Cold-Attuned Slam
solutions.interpretation: Support [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemRollingSlam|Rolling Slam]] with [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemColdInfusion|Cold Attunement]] so a legal physical Mace attack gains a meaningful Cold component. This is gain-as-extra, not conversion: improving the underlying weapon hit remains productive, while the support's penalties discourage an unfocused multi-element plan. The combat loop uses the broad slam for packs, allows the Cold portion to supply control naturally, and saves [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTimeFreeze|Time Freeze]] for a deliberate high-commitment hit against dangerous targets. Scale weapon physical DPS, Cold or elemental attack damage, and Cold penetration while checking that later supports remain compatible with the attack. The Chronomancer participates through a safe attack window rather than pretending to grant Cold damage. One-handed Mace and shield is attractive because the route does not require the largest possible two-handed impact; it also leaves more room to survive while Freeze buildup or Chill develops. Twisted Empyrean was discovered as a strong externally supported alternate, but the current catalog classifies its base as Kalguuran content, so this permanent-content artifact excludes it rather than silently bypassing policy.
solutions.defense: A shield complements gradual cold control; use temporal control before long attack commitments.
caveats: Cold Attunement grants extra Cold; it does not convert the physical hit.
unresolved: The catalog marks Twisted Empyrean as Kalguuran content, conflicting with its otherwise-current researched route; it is omitted under the seasonal exclusion rule.

solutions.title: Lightning-Attuned Impact
solutions.interpretation: Attach [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemLightningInfusion|Lightning Attunement]] to [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemRollingSlam|Rolling Slam]] to make Lightning damage part of a weapon-legal Mace hit without claiming full conversion. The route remains a hit build: sweep through packs with the slam, line up larger impacts during favorable Chronomancer tempo, and let [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyInevitableAgony|Inevitable Agony]] reward the hit size. Lightning Attunement penalizes other elemental damage, so prioritize a strong physical base that feeds the gained Lightning, then Lightning or elemental attack scaling and penetration instead of spreading investment across every element. This solution deliberately makes no Shock claim; dealing Lightning damage is carrier evidence, not proof of application. A one-handed Mace and shield supplies stability during the two-stage attack, while a two-handed version can pursue larger rolls if defensive recovery is sufficient. Phased Form and Temporal Rift can cover close-range mistakes, but they do not increase Lightning damage. Repository uniques surfaced during discovery were withheld because the report could not verify their live modifiers, leaving the support bridge as the publishable current route.
solutions.defense: Shield and temporal recovery help the committed slam sequence.
caveats: Lightning damage alone does not prove Shock application.

solutions.title: Chaos-Attuned Impact
solutions.interpretation: A high-base Mace attack becomes a Chaos route by linking [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemRollingSlam|Rolling Slam]] with [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemChaosInfusion|Chaos Attunement]]. The support adds Chaos rather than converting all physical damage, and its penalty to other damage asks the character to commit to the Chaos lane instead of building a rainbow hit. Use the slam as the regular clear and single-target carrier, with [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTimeFreeze|Time Freeze]] reserved for the moments when its long animation would be unsafe. [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyInevitableAgony|Inevitable Agony]] is relevant to the combined hit, not to any imagined Poison damage. Gear first for a strong weapon base, then Chaos attack scaling and ways to overcome enemy Chaos defenses; add Poison only as a separately enabled second plan. For defense, a shield reduces the cost of an experimental damage bridge, and Temporal Rift offers an escape after a badly placed slam. Nebuloch appeared in local unique retrieval, but the research did not independently confirm its current item text, so it is intentionally not used to justify this published solution.
solutions.defense: Favor shield-based durability while the support bridge carries offense.
caveats: Chaos Attunement is gain-as-extra, not conversion.
Chaos damage does not intrinsically apply Poison.

solutions.title: Molten Ignition
solutions.interpretation: Fire conversion and application are kept as separate steps: [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemMoltenBlast|Molten Blast]] supplies the Mace-delivered Fire hit, while [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemIgnitionThree|Ignite III]] supplies explicit Ignite capability. Molten Blast's projectile coverage and Ignite-duration interaction make it a natural clearing carrier, but neither feature is rewritten as unconditional application. Build enough Fire hit damage and Flammability/application reliability first, then invest in Ignite magnitude and duration; payoff supports belong only after the first Ignite is secured. [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable7|Apex of the Moment]] helps preserve distance and gives the slower Mace user a cleaner firing window, without multiplying the ailment. The play loop peppers packs with converted projectiles, checks that application is consistent, and uses close-range temporal recovery when enemies breach the firing line. A shield is a practical complement because the skill already supplies reach. Fire hit penetration should not be casually advertised as scaling the damage-over-time portion, and Inevitable Agony, if selected, belongs to the initial hit lane rather than the subsequent burn.
solutions.defense: Shield use and enemy slowing protect the ranged firing rhythm.
caveats: Payoff supports such as Fire Exposure require an Ignite and do not establish the first application.

solutions.title: Perfect-Strike Ignite
solutions.interpretation: This version turns the timed impact of [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemPerfectStrike|Perfect Strike]] into a strong Ignite carrier, but only because [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemIgnitionThree|Ignite III]] supplies the missing application mechanism. Wait for a controlled opening, release the high-conversion strike, then reposition while the ailment works; [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTimeFreeze|Time Freeze]] can create that opening against a target that would otherwise interrupt the timing. Scale the physical weapon base that feeds conversion, Fire hit contribution, application reliability, Ignite magnitude, and useful duration. The initial strike and the burn are distinct lanes: [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyInevitableAgony|Inevitable Agony]] can reward the hit, but its current tracked-loss mechanic is not fueled by Ignite ticks. Compared with Molten Blast, this route accepts worse coverage in exchange for one deliberate, larger application. A shield gives safer attempts; a two-handed Mace can raise the hit feeding the Ignite but magnifies missed timing. The old claim that Perfect Strike always Ignites is explicitly rejected, so removing the Ignite support would invalidate this interpretation rather than merely lower its damage.
solutions.defense: Use temporal control and a shield for reliable release timing, or accept higher two-handed risk.
caveats: Perfect Strike no longer always Ignites; the support is required here.

solutions.title: Heavy Bleed Windows
solutions.interpretation: Use [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemEarthquake|Earthquake]] as the physical Mace carrier and [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemLacerateThree|Bleed III]] as the explicit application layer, so a physical tag is never mistaken for inherent Bleed chance. Aftershock timing gives the build a deliberate setup/payoff cadence: establish the impact zone, keep the target controlled, and let the heavy physical hit apply the ailment. [[passive:passive_keystone_crimson_dance_|Crimson Assault]] is an optional build-defining keystone, not filler; its aggravated, short-duration Bleeds demand repeated strong applications and make duration management part of the loop. [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable7|Apex of the Moment]] helps hold enemies near the delayed impact, while the Chronomancer's hit tools only affect the initial strike—Bleed ticks do not feed Inevitable Agony by assumption. Scale weapon physical damage, Bleed magnitude, reliable application, and either duration or reapplication rate appropriate to the chosen keystone. A shield and Temporal Rift help survive near the delayed aftershock. The externally interesting Blistering Bond Fire/Bleed route remains absent because its patch-sensitive item semantics were not sufficiently represented locally or revalidated for publication.
solutions.defense: Shield defense and enemy slowing help keep targets in the delayed-impact area.
caveats: Crimson Assault materially changes duration and should not be treated as a free generic upgrade.

solutions.title: Physical Poison Crusher
solutions.interpretation: Keep the weapon physical: [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemRollingSlam|Rolling Slam]] supplies a legal Mace hit whose physical damage can contribute to Poison magnitude, and [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemEnvenom|Poison I]] supplies the actual Poison chance. That distinction avoids an unnecessary Chaos-conversion story and prevents carrier damage from being mistaken for application. Slam through packs to establish stacks, then use [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable7|Apex of the Moment]] to slow dangerous enemies while repeated committed hits refresh or add Poison according to the current stacking rules. Invest in the physical or Chaos contribution used by the ailment, explicit application reliability, Poison magnitude, duration, and sustainable attack cadence; hit penetration is not presented as equivalent to Poison scaling. [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemChaosInfusion|Chaos Attunement]] can be added as extra Chaos if its penalties suit the build, but it is an enhancer rather than the source of Poison. A shield helps maintain contact for repeated applications, and [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTemporalRift|Temporal Rift]] offers positional recovery after a slow sequence. Chronomancer controls the time available to apply Poison; it is not being credited with intrinsic ailment damage.
solutions.defense: Shield sustain plus Temporal Rift supports repeated close-range applications.
caveats: Physical damage contributes to magnitude but does not itself grant Poison chance.

solutions.title: Cold Impact Control
solutions.interpretation: Link [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemColdInfusion|Cold Attunement]] to [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemRollingSlam|Rolling Slam]] so the Mace hit genuinely contains Cold damage and can produce Chill. The support grants extra Cold rather than replacing physical damage, so a strong weapon base remains the foundation; scale the Cold component, Chill magnitude or effectiveness where available, and enemy Cold mitigation. Packs are handled with broad slams, while [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable7|Apex of the Moment]] supplies an independent Chronomancer slow that makes the long animation easier to commit to. These control effects are not assigned an unverified additive stacking formula. Against tougher targets, keep attacking to maintain meaningful Chill rather than assuming a token Cold portion reaches maximum effect. A one-handed Mace and shield is comfortable for the control-oriented plan, with [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTemporalRift|Temporal Rift]] reserved for repositioning after a mistimed sequence. Frost Nexus and Spreading Frost were considered but not used as first-Chill sources because their useful secondary effect depends on an already established Freeze. The route therefore has a short, explicit causal chain: Mace attack, extra Cold, then Chill.
solutions.defense: Shield defense and Temporal Rift complement the control-first rhythm.
caveats: Do not assert a specific stacking formula between Chill and Apex of the Moment.

solutions.title: Heavy Freeze Buildup
solutions.interpretation: Put [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemColdInfusion|Cold Attunement]] on [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemRollingSlam|Rolling Slam]] and treat Freeze as a buildup problem, not a binary reward for possessing a Cold tag. Large Mace hits make a sensible carrier once the support adds meaningful Cold damage; improve the weapon base, Cold contribution, Freeze buildup, and relevant Cold penetration so high-threshold targets are not ignored. The loop lands the staged slam, capitalizes only when a real Freeze occurs, and uses [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTimeFreeze|Time Freeze]] for a separate Chronomancer control window when buildup has not yet succeeded. The similarly named effects remain distinct—Time Freeze is not evidence that every weapon hit inflicts the ailment. A shield makes repeated buildup attempts safer, while a two-handed weapon may favor fewer, larger contributions at greater risk. [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTemporalRift|Temporal Rift]] can undo a bad melee commitment. Supports that merely let another damage type contribute to Freeze, or create an effect after Freeze, were rejected as initial application proof. This route promises a credible investment path, not guaranteed boss freezing from a negligible Cold component.
solutions.defense: Choose shield safety or larger two-handed buildup hits; retain a temporal escape.
caveats: Freeze success remains threshold-dependent, especially on bosses.

solutions.title: Fire-Fed Shock
solutions.interpretation: Wear [[unique:The Three Dragons||Solid Mask|The Three Dragons]] to redirect a Fire-hit ailment lane into Shock, then use [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemPerfectStrike|Perfect Strike]] as the high-impact Mace carrier. This is deliberately item-dependent: the helmet's replacement rules enable the unusual route and also give up ordinary ailment behavior, so it cannot be reduced to “Fire also Shocks.” Create a safe release window with [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable7|Apex of the Moment]], land the converted Fire hit, and scale the hit and the resulting Shock effectiveness according to the current ailment rules. The physical weapon base still matters because Perfect Strike converts from it. [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyInevitableAgony|Inevitable Agony]] rewards the hit itself and should not be described as a Shock multiplier. A shield makes the timed strike more reliable; a two-handed Mace offers a larger carrier but greater exposure. Lightning Attunement was discovered but not published as an alternate because the report found no separately verified first-Shock source for that chain. Likewise, Coursing Current and Lightning Exposure are not allowed to bootstrap an ailment they require. The route is coherent precisely because its unique supplies the named bridge.
solutions.defense: Use slowing and shield defense to land the timed carrier safely.
caveats: The unique changes normal ailment behavior; do not expect the ordinary Fire ailment lane.

solutions.title: Charged Electrocution Slam
solutions.interpretation: This route preserves every link in the chain: [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemRollingSlam|Rolling Slam]] is the legal Mace attack, [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemLightningInfusion|Lightning Attunement]] gives it Lightning damage, and [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemElectrocute|Electrocute]] lets that Lightning contribute to Electrocution buildup. Electrocute also prevents the supported skill from inflicting Shock, so the build accepts a control lane rather than claiming both ailments from one socket group. Sweep packs with the staged slam and use [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable7|Apex of the Moment]] to buy enough time for committed follow-up hits until buildup succeeds. Scale the physical base feeding extra Lightning, Lightning attack damage, and Electrocution buildup; do not call the support a conversion. [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable4|Phased Form]] is particularly useful while standing close enough to repeat slow attacks, and Temporal Rift can remove the paired delayed damage only when the corresponding Chronomancer package is actually allocated. Against resistant or high-threshold targets, treat Electrocution as earned control rather than guaranteed lockdown. If Shock is desired elsewhere, it needs a separate skill and independent application source, not a contradictory support claim on this attack.
solutions.defense: Phased Form and Temporal Rift can protect repeated close-range buildup attempts.
caveats: The supported attack cannot inflict Shock while Electrocute is linked.

setupAndPayoffRelationships: Forge Hammer object -> Skittering Stone minion
Mace attack -> extra Lightning -> Living Lightning minion

solutions.title: Skittering Forge
solutions.interpretation: Drive the Minion plan through a verified Mace object interaction: [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemForgeHammer|Forge Hammer]] creates the eligible earthen hammer, and [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SupportGemSkitteringStone|Skittering Stone I]] releases temporary stone Minions from that object. Skittering Stone is not generalized to every Mace attack. Place the hammer, use its recall or Warcry shatter rhythm, and let the temporary Minions occupy enemies while the player prepares the next cycle. [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTimeSnap|Time Snap]] can reset Forge Hammer's real cooldown when the tactical value warrants it, but it neither creates the object nor replaces the Warcry interaction. Decide whether the Mace hit or Minions receive primary scaling; splitting every point evenly risks weak versions of both, although Strength requirements provide some common ground. Area damage and cooldown rhythm favor the player lane, while Minion damage and duration favor the spawned lane. A shield is viable if the Minions carry meaningful pressure; a heavier Mace accepts more personal exposure and benefits from Temporal Rift. This is an integrated bridge, not a generic summon stapled onto a weapon build.
solutions.defense: Let temporary Minions create space; use shield or Temporal Rift during object setup.
caveats: Skittering Stone requires the verified eligible object and does not work generically with every Mace attack.

solutions.title: Living Lightning Crusher
solutions.interpretation: Turn [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemRollingSlam|Rolling Slam]] into a Minion trigger by first adding Lightning with [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SupportGemLightningInfusion|Lightning Attunement]], then linking [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SupportGemLivingLightning|Living Lightning]], whose creation condition is satisfied when the supported skill deals that Lightning damage. The ordering matters: Living Lightning does not make an unmodified physical Mace attack Lightning on its own. Slam packs to produce temporary chaining Minions, then reposition while they spread secondary pressure. Scale a strong weapon base and Lightning contribution if the player's hit is primary, or prioritize Minion output after maintaining enough reliable Lightning delivery to keep creation flowing. [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable7|Apex of the Moment]] helps the slow attacker remain safe during generation, but it does not buff Minions directly. A one-handed Mace and shield suits the hybrid better than chasing maximum personal hit damage at all costs, and Temporal Rift can rescue an overextended generation attempt. This route is mechanically distinct from Skittering Forge: it uses a damage-type prerequisite and on-hit creation rather than an earthen object and cooldown cycle.
solutions.defense: Shield durability supports repeated Minion generation from melee range.
priorities: choose player or Minion scaling emphasis
caveats: Living Lightning requires the supported skill to deal Lightning damage.

solutions.title: Tamed Beast Sidecar
solutions.interpretation: Treat the roll honestly as a hybrid. [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemRollingSlam|Rolling Slam]] remains the Mace-delivered primary attack, while [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemTameBeast|Tame Beast]] captures a qualifying Rare Beast and transforms into the skill that summons it as a reviving Companion. The Mace neither creates nor scales the Beast merely by being equipped. In play, maintain the captured Companion, use it as parallel pressure or distraction, and deliver physical slams during openings created by [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable7|Apex of the Moment]]. Gear must satisfy the capture and Spirit/capacity constraints as well as the weapon plan; choose a clear investment leader rather than assuming attack and Companion scaling coincide. A one-handed Mace and shield is the conservative choice because this route gains less from maximizing one enormous hit and benefits from staying alive while its ally works. [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTemporalRift|Temporal Rift]] supplies positional recovery when the melee half overextends. Rhoa Mount was explicitly rejected because its Bow/Spear restriction conflicts with Mace. No weapon-native causal bridge comparable to the Minion support chains was found, so the difficult assessment and unresolved integration gap are part of the result, not hidden weaknesses.
solutions.defense: One-handed Mace and shield support the intentionally split hybrid.
priorities: choose attack or Companion investment leader
caveats: The Companion is a sidecar, not a Mace-created entity.
unresolved: No current Mace-causes-Companion bridge was verified.

setupAndPayoffRelationships: Jagged Ground setup -> Shockwave Totem interaction
Volcanic Fissure -> allied Totem slam trigger

solutions.title: Fissure-and-Totem Relay
solutions.interpretation: Open with [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemVolcanicFissure|Volcanic Fissure]] to lay down Fire fissures, then place [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemShockwaveTotem|Shockwave Totem]]; its allied slams can trigger the established fissures while using the equipped Mace. This is a genuine setup/payoff relationship, not two unrelated damage buttons and not an inference from the generic Totemable tag. Rotate player slams, totem placement, and repositioning, using [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gem/SkillGemAscendancyTimeFreeze|Time Freeze]] when the setup would otherwise be interrupted. Scale the weapon and the current Totem-specific attack mechanics, Fire and area damage shared by the fissure package, and placement economy; do not rely on the obsolete assumption that ordinary supports modify the Totem attack as they once did. The proxy lets the Chronomancer spend more time controlling space, though the ascendancy is not claimed to grant Totem damage. A shield and Temporal Rift make the setup safer when the player must enter Mace range. Ancestral Bond is left to the alternate route because its Spirit reservation changes the whole resource plan rather than being a free extra recommendation.
solutions.defense: Use proxy pressure, shield defense, and Temporal Rift rather than face-tanking during setup.
caveats: Validate supports against the current post-change Shockwave Totem model.

solutions.title: Spirit-Bound Shockwave Totems
solutions.interpretation: Center the build on [[skill:Metadata/Items/Gems/SkillGemShockwaveTotem|Shockwave Totem]], which actually creates a Totem and attacks with equipped martial weapons, including the rolled Mace. Add [[passive:passive_keystone_ancestral_bond|Ancestral Bond]] only with an explicit resource plan: it doubles Totem Limit and removes the ordinary placement cost or Charge requirement, while each Totem reserves 75 Spirit. Place the expanded totem group, control enemies with [[passive:AscendancySorceress2Notable7|Apex of the Moment]], and reposition while the proxies perform the repeated slams. Scale the equipped weapon and current Totem-specific mechanics rather than socketing supports under an outdated attack model. Spirit reservation is a hard gearing constraint and competes with other persistent effects; it is not optional flavor. The route can use a shield because player attack damage is less central, giving the Chronomancer time to manage placement and Temporal Rift. Compared with the fissure relay, this is a resource-and-capacity build: its distinct payoff is additional active Totems, and its distinct failure mode is recommending the keystone without enough Spirit.
solutions.defense: Shield defense and proxy positioning reduce direct melee exposure.
caveats: Ancestral Bond requires 75 Spirit reserved per Totem in the researched current version.
